showIp: Show the address for this request
ipWaiting: The address appears here after you ask.
ipMissing: This request did not include a readable address.
estimateNote: Zoom and OS scaling change the ratio, so this is not a measurement of the panel.
macNote: An iPad in desktop mode can send a Mac user-agent, so a macOS label means the browser reported macOS.

hub.name: My device
hub.blurb: Screen, browser, language, time zone, and dark mode in this tab.
hub.title: My device — cv.cm
hub.description: Screen size, browser, language, time zone, and dark mode reported by this tab, plus a button to show the IP address of this request. Nothing is saved.
hub.lede: Screen size, browser, language, time zone, and dark mode reported by this tab, plus a button to show the IP address of this request. Nothing is saved.
hub.readBody: This page lists what the tab can already see. Each reading has its own page, including the language, the time zone, and whether dark mode is on.
hub.leaveBody: Screen, browser, language, time zone, color scheme, and user agent are read in this tab and are not uploaded. The IP address is requested from this site only after you click, then shown here and not stored.
hub.q1: What can this tab see without a click?
hub.a1: The screen size, the browser name, the user-agent string, the language, the time zone, and the color scheme. The IP address waits for the button.
hub.q2: What does this column refuse to read?
hub.a2: No city, no WebRTC connection, no canvas, fonts, GPU, or battery, and no fingerprint hash.
hub.a3: No. The readings stay in this tab. The IP response is not written to a database.
hub.q4: Why does the IP address wait for a click?
hub.a4: The address is requested only when you ask, and it is not stored.
hub.a5: Each page explains one reading. This page only summarizes them and links across.

ip.name: What is my IP address
ip.blurb: The public address of this request, after you ask.
ip.title: What is my IP address — cv.cm
ip.description: How to read the public IP address of this request. The address is shown only after you ask, it is not stored, and this page does not look up a city.
ip.lede: How to read the public IP address of this request. The address is shown only after you ask, it is not stored, and this page does not look up a city.
ip.readBody: A public address is the one this request used to reach cv.cm. A private LAN address, such as one that starts with 192.168, stays inside the network and is not what this page shows. The examples 203.0.113.10 and 2001:db8::1 are documentation addresses, not yours.
ip.leaveBody: You do not upload an address. The click asks this site for the address it already saw on the request. The response is not stored.
ip.q1: Is the value, once shown, the public address of this request?
ip.a1: Yes. It is the address this request used to reach cv.cm. A VPN or carrier NAT can change it. It is not a private address such as 192.168.
ip.a2: This page does not look up a city, a region, or a map.
ip.a3: No. The response is shown in this tab and is not written down.
ip.a4: You see the one this connection used. This page does not open a second connection to force the other.
ip.q5: Does this look for a WebRTC leak?
ip.a5: No. This page does not open a WebRTC connection, so it does not look for another address behind a VPN.

browser.name: What browser am I using
browser.blurb: Name and version reported by this tab.
browser.title: What browser am I using — cv.cm
browser.description: Browser name and version reported by this tab, and why client hints and the user-agent string can disagree.
browser.lede: Browser name and version reported by this tab, and why client hints and the user-agent string can disagree.
browser.readBody: Client hints can name the browser and a full version. The user-agent string is older and, in Chrome, often freezes the minor version. When both exist, this page prefers the hint.
browser.leaveBody: The name and version are read in this tab. They are not uploaded.
browser.q1: Why can the version disagree with the user-agent string?
browser.a1: Client hints can carry a full version. Chrome's user-agent string often freezes the minor version.
browser.q2: Do other sites already receive this?
browser.a2: Every request already sends a user-agent. This page does not send an extra copy.
browser.a3: It is a coarse label shared by many people. This page does not combine signals into an identifier.
browser.a4: From the mobile client hint when the browser provides one. Otherwise the page uses the platform in the string.
browser.q5: How is this different from the user-agent page?
browser.a5: This page names the browser and version. The user-agent page shows the raw string.

screen.name: What is my screen resolution
screen.blurb: Screen size and window size in CSS pixels.
screen.title: What is my screen resolution — cv.cm
screen.description: The screen size and window size this browser reports, in CSS pixels, and what device pixel ratio does and does not measure.
screen.lede: The screen size and window size this browser reports, in CSS pixels, and what device pixel ratio does and does not measure.
screen.readBody: The first number is the screen size this browser reports, in CSS pixels. The window can be smaller. At a device pixel ratio of 2, 1920×1080 CSS pixels are about 3840×2160 device pixels. Zoom and OS scaling change the ratio, so that product is an estimate, not a measurement of the panel.
screen.leaveBody: The sizes are read in this tab. They are not uploaded.
screen.q1: What is the difference between the screen and the window?
screen.a1: The screen is the display size the browser reports. The window is this page's viewport and can be smaller.
screen.q2: What does the device pixel ratio mean?
screen.a2: CSS pixels times the ratio are an estimate of device pixels. At a ratio of 2, 1920×1080 is about 3840×2160. Zoom and OS scaling change the ratio, so this is not a measurement of the panel.
screen.q3: Is this size an HTTP header?
screen.a3: No. The page reads it in the tab. It is not sent with the request unless some other script reads it and sends it.
screen.q4: Why can this differ from the monitor's advertised size?
screen.a4: OS scaling can make a 4K panel report a smaller CSS size. The browser reports the scaled size.
screen.a5: Turning a phone swaps the width and height the browser reports. Refresh the reading by loading the page again after you rotate.

ua.name: What is my user agent
ua.blurb: The raw string this browser sends.
ua.title: What is my user agent — cv.cm
ua.description: The user-agent string this browser sends. It is not your IP address, and it is not stored.
ua.lede: The user-agent string this browser sends. It is not your IP address, and it is not stored.
ua.readBody: The string names a browser, an engine, and an operating system. It does not name an IP address, a person, or a city. An iPad in desktop mode can send a Mac user-agent, so a macOS label means the browser reported macOS.
ua.leaveBody: The string is read in this tab. Copy stays on the clipboard you choose. It is not uploaded.
ua.a1: A line the browser sends with requests. It names the browser, the engine, and the operating system.
ua.a2: Not your IP address, your name, or a city.
ua.q3: Why can Chrome's string look reduced?
ua.a3: Chrome often sends a reduced string, so the minor version may not match the browser's own About box.
ua.q4: Can I copy it for a bug report?
ua.a4: Yes. Copy the string and paste it into the report. This page does not send it anywhere.
ua.q5: Does changing the string make me private?
ua.a5: No. Changing the string is not a privacy tool. An iPad in desktop mode can also send a Mac user-agent, so a macOS label means the browser reported macOS.

language.name: What language is my browser
language.blurb: The language list this tab reports.
language.title: What language is my browser — cv.cm
language.description: The language list this browser reports, in the order it prefers them. Nothing is uploaded.
language.lede: The language list this browser reports, in the order it prefers them. Nothing is uploaded.
language.readBody: The first tag is the language this tab asks for. The rest are fallbacks. A tag such as zh-CN names a language and a region, not the city you are in.
language.leaveBody: The list is read in this tab. It is not uploaded.
language.q1: Is the first language the one sites see?
language.a1: Sites can read this list in the page, and the request also sends an Accept-Language header. This page shows the list from the tab.
language.q2: Does a region tag mean I am in that place?
language.a2: No. zh-CN means the language preference, not a city lookup.
language.q3: Can I have more than one language?
language.a3: Yes. The list is in the order the browser prefers them.
language.a4: No. The list stays in this tab.
language.q5: How is this different from the browser page?
language.a5: That page names the browser. This page names the languages it asks for.

zone.name: What is my time zone
zone.blurb: The IANA zone and the current UTC offset.
zone.title: What is my time zone — cv.cm
zone.description: The time zone name and the UTC offset this browser is using right now. Nothing is uploaded.
zone.lede: The time zone name and the UTC offset this browser is using right now. Nothing is uploaded.
zone.readBody: The name is an IANA zone, such as Asia/Shanghai. The offset is for this moment, so daylight saving is already included. It is a setting of this browser, not a city lookup. The timezone converter turns one wall clock into another.
zone.leaveBody: The zone and the offset are read in this tab. They are not uploaded.
zone.q1: Is the offset the same all year?
zone.a1: Not where daylight saving moves the clock. The offset shown is for right now.
zone.a2: No. A zone such as Asia/Shanghai is a clock setting. This page does not look up a city.
zone.a3: It turns one wall-clock time into another zone. This page only names the zone this tab is using.
zone.a4: No. The name and the offset stay in this tab.
zone.a5: Not by itself. The zone follows the clock setting of this device, not the network address.

appearance.name: Is dark mode on
appearance.blurb: The color scheme and motion preference this tab reports.
appearance.title: Is dark mode on — cv.cm
appearance.description: Whether this browser prefers a dark or light color scheme, and whether it asks sites to reduce motion. Nothing is uploaded.
appearance.lede: Whether this browser prefers a dark or light color scheme, and whether it asks sites to reduce motion. Nothing is uploaded.
appearance.readBody: Dark means the browser asked for a dark scheme. Light means it asked for a light one. No preference means it did not choose. cv.cm itself stays light. Reduced motion is a separate request about animation, not about the color of the room.
appearance.leaveBody: These preferences are read in this tab. They are not uploaded.
appearance.q1: Does dark here mean cv.cm is in dark mode?
appearance.a1: No. The reading is the browser's preference. cv.cm stays light.
appearance.q2: Is this a measurement of the room?
appearance.a2: No. It is a setting. It does not see the room.
appearance.a3: A request that sites use less animation. It is separate from dark or light.
appearance.a4: No. The preferences stay in this tab.
appearance.q5: Will this change if I change the system setting?
appearance.a5: Reload the page after you change it. The reading is whatever the browser reports then.
